Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

sharedAssociations.basis: The imported Atakapa and Atakapa-Ishak records cover overlapping Gulf Coast regions of southeastern Texas and southwestern Louisiana. Their date ranges are map snapshots, not separate peoples.

scopeNotes: The broader 1650 to 1783 polygons reach beyond the core Louisiana range. Association permits a broad cultural narrative, not approval of every imported boundary.
Grand Bayou’s Atakapa-Ishak Chawasha record is geographically and historically distinct and is not attached to this card. Akokisa retains its own researched narrative.
The older community website has unrelated injected commercial text. It was not selected as a public citation. Unsupported origin claims for foods and zydeco are not adopted.
The historical exonym’s hostile meaning is not proof of cannibalism. Outdated claims that only nine descendants existed are not treated as a census or extinction finding.
Basket 22/8845 has a documented collection history; E360927 has competing attributions. The latter is included to explain uncertainty, not as a secure Atakapa masterpiece.
Caplen page 469 was read in indexed text after the full PDF exceeded the web reader’s size limit. No skeletal analysis or direct inspection of remains was performed.
The 1932 dictionary pages 4 and 5 were read; the entire dictionary and the full 2022 grammar were not. Digital resource descriptions were checked, but no fluency outcome is inferred.
Modern recognition status and individual ancestry are not adjudicated. Independent review, geometry review and depth certification remain pending.
